name: Ideal QAOA versus classical controls on 64 toy Module-LWE examples
cohort: The same 64 previously generated toy Module-LWE development examples, all retained
encoding: LLL-reduced 8-dimensional secret/error embedding; Babai-centered coefficients [-2,-1,0,+1]; 2 bits per coefficient; 16 qubits
coverage_audit_before_run: The previously proposed two-bit window contains at least one known exact optimum on all 64 cases; no window adjustment or instance filtering performed.
angle_objective: Minimize normalized expected squared decoding cost; no reference optimum or planted secret enters parameter fitting

instance_tuning.starts: trained global angle plus three prespecified starts

classical_controls: Uniform sampling with replacement in the identical binary box
CBD(eta=2) secret sampling with optimal modular lift
hybrid_rule: Retain Babai's candidate and replace it only with a strictly lower public cost; ties retain the incumbent
secret_recovery_rule: Evaluate the returned minimum-cost candidate, with ties resolved by earliest sample or retained Babai incumbent
limitations: Exploratory comparison on one tiny parameter set and previously inspected development instances, not a final unseen evaluation.
One QAOA layer and this specific encoding/parameter procedure; no general conclusion about all QAOA variants.
Analytic p=1 energy optimization is performed classically; its effort is recorded and excluded from the displayed shot budget.
Equal samples do not mean equal runtime, energy consumption, or full computational effort.
Classical secret sampling exploits the known small-secret distribution and is not confined to the binary box; uniform box sampling isolates the same-space comparison.
Classical local refinement is over the full integer coefficient lattice, with explicit candidate-evaluation counts.
No noise or hardware execution. CVP success is separate from planted-secret recovery.
